https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/n.title: ‘It’s a new world. It’s a little fascistic. And it needs a different response’: U2 on 50 years together – and their undimmed faith in humanity
https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/n.author: Alexis Petridis
https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/n.text:
La Petite Maison, in Nice, has a certain reputation as a five-star celebrity haunt. Beyoncé eats here. So do Elton John, Tom Cruise, Harry Styles and Leonardo DiCaprio, their meals presided over by the restaurant’s founder, Nicole, variously described in print as “eccentric”, “unique” and “truculent” (she’s standing by the entrance when I arrive, and suffice to say, doesn’t look like someone you’d much enjoy being on the wrong side of).
It’s enough of a celebrity haunt that the arrival of U2 – still incontrovertibly one of the biggest bands in the world 40 years after they could first reasonably have called themselves such – causes barely a murmur of interest among their fellow lunchtime diners. Then again, Bono is a regular. He was eating on the outdoor terrace the night of Nice’s terrorist attack, on Bastille Day in 2016, in which 86 people were killed. “I climbed through that window and hid under there,” he nods, pointing to a table at the rear of the restaurant. “Nicole,” he adds, “didn’t hide.”
It’s a very plush spot for a rehearsal lunch break, which is what my meeting with U2 amounts to. All the band’s members own houses nearby and the interview has been squeezed in among preparations for a secret gig at London’s Tate Modern, including songs they recorded in collaboration with Brian Eno – “to celebrate the great man and our collaborative history”, as the Edge puts it. The show, on Tuesday night, was the latest event in what is proving a packed year. There were the EPs Days of Ash and Easter Lily, the latter filled with songs of a spiritual bent, the former with righteous anger and invective variously inspired by the war in Ukraine, the genocide in Palestine – Bono recently caused uproar in Israel by comparing comments made by the country’s national security minister to Heinrich Himmler – and the Trump administration. (It arrived a month after ICE’s shooting of Renee Good, the subject of its opening track, American Obituary.)
There is also their first album of new material in nearly nine years, Carnaval de Luz – of which more later – and an accompanying world tour. And there was a performance at Dublin’s Mount Temple Comprehensive, to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Larry Mullen sticking a card on the school’s noticeboard (“drummer seeks musicians to form band”). U2 were greeted enthusiastically by an audience of current pupils waving homemade signs. Some were apparently suitably reverential: “Welcome home”; “Truly it’s a beautiful day”. Others were, perhaps, a little less so: “Which one of you is Inhaler’s dad?”; “When are Oasis on?”
Impertinent calls for them to cede the stage to the Gallaghers notwithstanding, the gig at their old school has made U2’s members think about their early days. It wasn’t so strange that they formed a band, muses Adam Clayton – it was, after all, the punk era, and plenty of other teenagers had the same idea. It was that, from the start, U2’s aims seemed slightly different. “We thought longevity for our band was an important goal,” he says, “which was the absolute opposite of the punk thing. In school in the 70s, we’d been faced with the petrol crisis, the economic crisis, worrying about what you were going to do. I think we thought: if we’ve got this thing, let’s just do it for as long as we can.”
“I remember that period when we first started to look for a record deal,” says the Edge. “We were actively impatient; we had a great level of expectation. It didn’t occur to us that this was preposterous. We were 16, 17, 18 and we expected to get a record deal. I think the clue’s in the title of the first album, Boy. It was a sort of examination of innocence and naivety, and those things are so important: they give you the sense that anything is possible, that change can happen, that you can be a huge band. It allowed us to think about global success, when there was almost no evidence that it was possible.”
What seems almost impossible is that U2 are still here, half a century later, with the same four members: there are doubtless other bands who can claim the same thing, but you struggle to think of one. That they have survived intact is down to what Bono calls “the soviet” – a democracy in which songwriting credits are always shared equally and everything is decided by committee.
Watching them interact over Madame Nicole’s butterflied prawns and pissaladière, you get a vague sense of how “the soviet” might work – occasionally, after Bono offers a long answer that digresses into quotations from books, songs and the Bible, another member of the band steps in and effectively grounds it, summarising what he’s just said in more direct terms. But nonetheless, there’s no getting around the fact that an equitable division of power is supposed to be a disastrous way to run a band. As Bruce Springsteen said when he inducted U2 into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2005: “I believe they actually practise some form of democracy – toxic poison in a band’s head!”
“I think if we really understood how it worked, we’d have moved out of the rock’n’roll business and into political advice,” says Mullen. “You have to be able to go into a room and share and be open to most circumstances.”
“It’s got harder as time’s gone on,” says Bono. “Because, as Marianne Faithfull would say in situations like this: ‘Never underestimate the male ego, darling.’ Students of male psychology will tell you that as men lose power, be that physical, sexual, mental, you make up for it by flexing.” He laughs, saying that when his own father reached that point, “he started sleeping with an iron bar under his pillow”, and illustrates this with a story about U2’s peers in the late 70s Irish rock scene, the Virgin Prunes. “As an art prank, they came by one night and wrapped our car up in hankies and powder, then threw eggs when I went to the window. Da thought we were being attacked and the fucking iron bar came out and he’s off down the road chasing them. But our rehearsals rarely get to that level. Very rarely.”
Successful democracy or not, this year’s flurry of activity comes at the end of a lengthy period of turbulence for U2. Bono and the Edge’s flop Broadway musical about Spider-Man, in 2011; the misguided launch of 2014’s Songs of Innocence when they invaded everyone’s iTunes libraries; the cool reaction afforded that album and its successor, Songs of Experience; Bono suffering both a bike crash in 2014 that left him with umpteen broken bones and facial trauma, and open heart surgery two years later. There were triumphs along the way, not least the Innocence and Experience and Joshua Tree tours, which had a combined gross of $543m. But by the time U2 played their 2023-24 residency at the Las Vegas Sphere without Mullen – recovering from neck surgery that looked like it could end his drumming career – there were rumblings about the band’s future, not least within U2 themselves.
“U2 is the four members of the band,” says the Edge, firmly. “I think that doesn’t mean we would stop making music if somebody left, but I think it would be a very different kind of group. We definitely would acknowledge that it was a U2 part two, rather than the same thing. I’m not sure we’d be sitting here if Larry wasn’t ready to play.”
And yet Mullen is here, looking in impressively chiselled rude health, and U2’s new album sounds noticeably more confident and, well, U2-ish than Songs of Innocence or Songs of Experience, both of which carried the faint sense of a band struggling to work out where they fitted into the 21st-century landscape. There were clumsy lunges for pop contemporaneity – Auto-Tuned vocals, songwriter-for-hire Ryan Tedder in the credits – and moments that sounded less like U2 than they did Coldplay. “The coherent many have overpowered the transcendent,” offers Bono, carefully: by contrast, on Carnaval de Luz, the Edge says one of their aims was “to make music only U2 could make”.
It features a duet with Dolly Parton that is now the last song the ailing country star – or, as Bono calls her, “the last thing all Americans agreed on” – ever recorded. “To sing alongside her is to be somewhat embarrassed, and that’s not false modesty,” he says of the experience of duetting with a vocalist whose skills he compares to those of Pakistani Qawwali master Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan. And there’s The Mirror Maker (Rosalía), a song in praise of the titular Spanish singer, replete with a falsetto vocal that mimics her operatic flourishes, which apparently required a meeting of the aforementioned soviet before it could go ahead.
“Just to fling the idea about and say: can we really do this?” says Bono. “I’ve been a fan for ages. She’s in the territory we were in – Catholicism, the saints, love for God – but it was a little bit embarrassing that she became so popular: like, great, U2 cop on to Rosalía just as she’s becoming the biggest star on the planet.” He ended up texting the singer to let her know what they had done. “I had to explain to one of her friends that I know that we were not, in fact, stalkers. But she was very humorous about it. She said, ‘I don’t have to sing on this, do I?’ And I said no, no, how on earth could we ask you to sing a song about you? That said, we got Johnny Cash to sing The Wanderer [on 1993’s Zooropa], and that was about him.”
“But it didn’t actually have his name in the title,” frowns Clayton. “It wasn’t called Johnny Cash: The Wanderer.”
The emotional tone of Carnaval de Luz is noticeably different from either of the EPs that preceded it, the anger of Days of Ash replaced by calls for community and a kind of defiant joy. “The news can’t break us,” as a song called Superficiality puts it.
“It’s not fiddling while Rome burns, it’s taking the fiddle off Nero and playing a better tune,” notes Bono, very Bono-ishly. “These divils must not control our mood.”
Bono says these are “exceptional times”. He is an activist who has never been averse to breaking bread with US politicians whose views evidently don’t align with his own. In the early 00s, he famously talked the Republican senator Jesse Helms, a virulent homophobe, into supporting funding to combat Aids. He lobbied George W Bush on debt relief for developing countries, and corralled a load of corporate suits into supporting the Product Red charity initiative. But he has been noticeably absent from the White House during the second Trump presidency: an administration that in 2025 disrupted the very Aids programme Bono helped to initiate.
“There’s a permission you need to feel to do a certain task,” he says, “and if you feel it spiritually. You feel like: I think I might be able to help here.” With the Trump administration, “I have been invited, but I know I’m not up to that, I don’t have the ability to negotiate [with them], it’s too much.” Bono says he doesn’t have “a plan, a strategy for successful action, a particular original idea I could get past them. Maybe just leave that to someone else. I don’t feel … the leading, is that the word? That thing where you think you know what to do.”
Mullen picks up the thread. “When money was taken away from Aids, from people in Africa, I think to be honest you were in a state of complete shock and dismay at what you were seeing. And these things take enormous amounts of time and energy and you can’t do everything, you can only do a certain amount.”
Is he saying he thinks this is a fundamentally different situation than what he’d encountered with right-wing politicians in previous administrations?
“Yes, I do,” says Bono. “It’s a new world. This is different. There’s a whiff, there’s a honk, and we’re all just trying to discern it. There’s a brand new dance and we do know its name,” he says, paraphrasing David Bowie’s Fashion. “It’s a little … fascistic. And it needs a different response.”
He talks about a meeting he had with Demis Hassabis, a Nobel prize-winning AI researcher. “Maybe one of the cleverest people on the planet,” who suggested that “unless there’s an exponential change in human behaviour and how we get on with each other and how we cooperate and reorganise to face the challenges of the world, like the climate crisis or whatever … we’re in deep trouble”. He says he still genuinely believes that rock music has a role to play in bringing people together, calling their upcoming tour “a no-holds-barred fight for a great night out”.
That’s despite a song on Carnaval de Luz called The Greatest Show on Earth, which you could take as a eulogy for U2’s imperial phase in the 80s and 90s, or for pop’s once-central, now-diminished role in culture. “We were once the greatest show on earth,” he sings, a line which apparently caused some consternation among U2’s ranks.
“Everyone was going: ‘You’re not going to sing that, are you?’,” he laughs. “Edge was saying: ‘How about: we could still be the greatest show on earth?’ Adam said: ‘What about: I think we’re the greatest show on earth?’ But I know how I feel when I sing it. The feeling of grasping that nettle – look what might have been – gives you hope.”
That time, he says, he overrode the objections of the soviet and got his own way. But it happens a lot less than you’d think, and perhaps that’s for the best. “I genuinely fantasise that one day these lads will actually just do what they’re told, but at this point, I’m giving up on that fantasy,” the Edges smiles, as U2 head for the rehearsal room. “I just don’t think it’s going to happen. And thank God, because if they started doing what they’re told, there’d be an absolutely shite album.”
Carnaval de Luz is released 13 November via Island. U2’s world tour begins 23 February at Estadio GNP Seguros, Mexico City, and includes three dates at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, London, 18-22 June

https://taz.de/Performance-Festival-Unid.author: Tom Mustroph
https://taz.de/Performance-Festival-Unid.text:
Performance-Festival „Unidram“ Potsdam: Ein Tapetenwechsel mal ohne Schwerkraft
Das Potsdamer Performance-Festival „Unidram“ ist spezialisiert auf visuelle Kunst mit wenigen Worten. Körper und Räume werden hier magisch verwandelt.
Kunst darf, ja sie soll sogar unsere Wahrnehmungen verrücken. Sehr gut klappt das derzeit beim Festival „Unidram“ in Potsdam. Dort sah man an den ersten beiden Tagen Menschen einfach durch Wände verschwinden. Häuser im gedehnten Zeitlupenmodus einstürzen und sich melancholisch von Wänden abrollende Tapeten, an denen sie eigentlich kleben. So geschehen beim Materialtheaterstück „Staub“ des Stuttgarter O-Teams, das für seine aufwendig gestalteten Bühnenräume bekannt ist.
Der gelernte Akrobat Tobias Wegner setzte mit seinem Kultstück „Leo“ noch einen drauf. In einem raffinierten Arrangement aus einem Raum, in dem der Künstler vor allem am Boden liegend agierte und einem um 90 Grad gekippten Projektionsraum, gerieten die Gesetze der Schwerkraft außer Kraft. Denn hob der im Realraum flach am Boden liegende Akteur mal schnell die Beine, so schien er im daneben platzierten Projektionsraum zwar mit dem Rücken an der Wand zu kleben – vom Boden hatten sich seine Füße aber definitiv gelöst.
Wegner reizte die um 90 Grad verschobenen Schwerkraftverhältnisse auch mit Wasser aus, das plötzlich waagerecht schwappte, und Gegenständen, die in der Horizontalen zurückkehrten. Auch die Grenzen zwischen Zwei- und Dreidimensionalität lösten sich auf. Denn der Akrobat konnte sich auf einen seitwärts an die Wand gemalten Stuhl einfach setzen oder sich an einem ebenfalls gezeichneten Fensterflügel die Wand entlang hochziehen.
Unidram Festival
Unidram Festival, noch bis 7. November 2026, Potsdam, „Kultur-Areal Schiffbauergasse“
https://www.unidram.de
Schweben im Zwillingsuniversum
Man wusste oft nicht, worüber man mehr staunen sollte: über die akrobatischen Fähigkeiten des Performers, der liegend so perfekt agierte, dass die Bewegungen in dem um 90 Grad gekippten Projektraum ungemein natürlich aussahen, oder über die Effekte des Schwebens und Fliegens im Zwillingsuniversum.
Dass „Leo“ überhaupt bei Unidram gelandet war, glich ebenfalls einem magischen Akt. Denn eigentlich war „Violent“, die wilde Bildverwandlungsshow der bretonischen Sociéteé Protectrice de Petites Ideés, als Eröffnungsproduktion geplant. Dann aber musste die Gruppe wegen eines Unfalls absagen. „Freitag früh um neun hatten wir die Information, nachmittags um vier die Lösung“, sagte Festival-Co-Kurator Jens-Uwe Sprengel der taz.
Möglich war es nur aufgrund des riesigen Netzwerks, das sich die Verantwortlichen in den mehr als drei Jahrzehnten ihres Wirkens aufgebaut haben; und auch aufgrund der Akzeptanz, die sie als verlässliche Partner in der internationalen Szene besitzen. „Wir haben dann den Sonnabend genutzt, um komplett alles durchzugehen, von Übernachtungen, Shuttle-Service und Verpflegung bis hin zu Werbung und Tickets“, erzählt Sprengel. Montag war Aufbau, Dienstag die erste Vorstellung.
Tanzen auf der Treppe
Beim Festival geht es mit (fast) wortloser, aber die Augen und die Ohren schier verwundernder Körper-, Klang- und Raumkunst weiter. Sprengel freut sich besonders auf die installative Reise in den einstigen New Yorker-Vergnügungspark Coney Island Beach mit der Produktion „Dreamland“ des kanadischen Théatre Rude Ingeniérie (5.–7. November) und die opulente Musikperformance „Spring Is Possible“ der belgischen Gruppe bodybody (7. November). Ein besonderes Experiment stellt die auf einer extra neu gebauten fünf Meter hohen Treppe inszenierte Klang-Tanz-Performance „Meta“ der iranisch-niederländischen Oriantheatre Dance Company (7. November) dar.
Die insgesamt neun Produktionen des fünftägigen Festivals weisen sehr markante künstlerische Handschriften auf. Sie alle aber laden zum Sich-verzaubern-Lassen ein, mal auf die sehr subtile, mal auf die schier überwältigende Art.
Gemeinsam für freie Presse
Die taz gehört zu 100 Prozent ihren Leser:innen und ist damit nicht nur konzernfrei, sondern auch kostenfrei zugänglich. Alle Artikel stellen wir frei zur Verfügung, ohne Paywall. Gerade in diesen Zeiten müssen Einordnungen und Informationen allen zugänglich sein. Unsere Leser:innen müssen nichts bezahlen, wissen aber, dass kritischer, unabhängiger Journalismus nicht aus dem Nichts entsteht. Dafür sind wir sehr dankbar. Damit wir auch morgen noch unseren Journalismus machen können, brauchen wir mehr Unterstützung für taz zahl ich. Dank Ihnen haben wir nun die 50.000 erreicht. So viele unterstützen freiwillig und regelmäßig. Noch nicht dabei? Werden Sie jetzt Teil der Community! Jetzt unterstützen

Journaliste et créateur du média en ligne « AOC », Sylvain Bourmeau est l’auteur de l’essai « Ils ne sont pas d’extrême droite, ils font l’extrême droite ». Il y décrit comment les mécanismes professionnels des médias et l’abandon de principes comme la vérification des faits créent un terrain favorable à l’idéologie du Rassemblement national.
Parmi ceux qui ne sont pas d’extrême droite mais qui la font, vous pointez les journalistes politiques. En quoi leur traitement du mouvement social en cours participe-t-il à ce phénomène ?
Sylvain Bourmeau
Journaliste et créateur du média en ligne « AOC »
On peut presque mettre en regard le cadrage qu’opère le pouvoir exécutif en choisissant de répondre par la répression policière au mouvement social avec le cadrage médiatique qu’opèrent la plupart des médias qui préfèrent s’intéresser à longueur de journée et de colonnes de journaux à l’aspect sécuritaire de ce mouvement.

https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.title: Who is Kozo Tashima, the Japanese official running for FIFA presidency?
https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/11.text:
Who is Kozo Tashima, the Japanese official running for FIFA presidency?
Tashima has served as a football player, coach and bureaucrat and has a reputation for being a safe pair of hands.
Kozo Tashima first started playing football after watching the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, and since then he has dedicated his life to developing the sport’s growth in Japan.
The 68-year-old is set to become the first person from Japan to run for the FIFA presidency after announcing he would stand against Gianni Infantino in football’s governing body’s election in March.
Tashima has served as a football player, coach and bureaucrat and has a reputation for being a safe pair of hands.
He rarely makes headlines, and one of the few times he appeared outside the sport pages was when he became one of the first public figures in Japan to contract coronavirus in March 2020.
He spent time studying at the German Sport University Cologne and said the experience changed the way he saw sport’s purpose in society.
He says his decision to run for the FIFA presidency was based on a belief that “in this age of business and money, sport must firmly uphold its integrity”.
“The worst thing would be if he [Infantino] were to continue without an election,” he told reporters after announcing his candidacy.
“I feel this is a test of whether FIFA has the ability to cleanse itself.”
Tashima was born in southern Kumamoto and captained his team to the title in Japan’s prestigious national high school championship.
With no professional football in the country at the time, he had ambitions of becoming a PE teacher and enrolled at a university, where he was called up to play for Japan’s full national team.
He joined a club in Japan’s amateur league after graduating but soon retired as a player and went to Germany to study to become a coach.
He described his “profound shock” at the players’ superior skills and the way football was viewed there.
“Even back in 1980, the training in Germany was hugely scientific and systematic,” he said.
“Everything seemed like a different world from Japan, and it was a big culture shock for me.”
Experienced hand
Tashima returned home determined to use what he had learned in Germany and help develop Japanese football.
He coached a university team before joining the Japan Football Association (JFA), where he worked on development programmes and coached the country’s national teams at various youth levels.
He rose through the JFA ranks and was elected president in 2016, while also serving on the Asian Football Confederation executive committee and the FIFA Council.
His reign as JFA chief saw him fire Japan coach Vahid Halilhodzic two months before the 2018 World Cup in Russia.
Halilhodzic, who was unpopular with the players, was replaced by Akira Nishino, and Japan reached the last 16, where they were eliminated by Belgium.
“Some people told me that I wasn’t the one who hired Halilhodzic so it wouldn’t be my fault if the team lost,” Tashima said.
“But as president, all the responsibility lay with me.”
Tashima stepped down as JFA chief in 2024 and was named honorary president.
He said he had decided to run for the FIFA presidency to “contribute to the further development of world football”.
Tashima said he was troubled by FIFA’s shock decision to lift a ban for United States player Folarin Balogun at this year’s World Cup, following an intervention by US President Donald Trump.
He said he also had a problem with the travel restrictions placed on Iran’s World Cup team by American authorities.
Tashima, who has the JFA’s backing, said his presidency bid was “not about winning or losing”.
“What matters is sharing with the world the integrity that Japan’s football has built over the years,” he said.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: The New York Times minimiza entrevista de Flávio Bolsonaro e desmente teses de fraude na eleição e perseguição
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O jornal estadunidense The New York Times refutou todas as teorias conspiratórias do senador e candidato derrotado à Presidência do Brasil Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), que fugiu para os Estados Unidos no dia 27 de outubro, em entrevista publicada nesta quinta-feira (5).
Anunciada como um grande evento por aliados do bolsonarista, a entrevista de 75 minutos foi conduzida por Ana Ionova, correspondente do jornal para o Brasil e os países vizinhos, rendeu poucas e curtas aspas ao longo do texto e já começa desmentindo o ex-candidato.
“De Miami, Flávio Bolsonaro insiste em alegações infundadas de fraude eleitoral e planeja influenciar a política do país à distância, mesmo que seu partido não esteja contestando os resultados”, diz o subtítulo do texto publicado pelo The New York Times.
Na entrevista, Flávio Bolsonaro repetiu a tese de fraude eleitoral na eleição presidencial, dizendo que a vitória de Lula seria “matematicamente impossível”, além de apresentar alegações sobre manipulação de votos e falha de segurança na sala onde os computadores contabilizam os votos, no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).
O jornal destacou que estas são alegações “já desmentidas” e demarcou as falas como um eco de “teorias da conspiração que seu pai outrora propagava sobre as urnas eletrônicas do Brasil, um sistema que especialistas internacionais consideram um dos mais seguros do mundo”.
O texto destaca que a campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro também pediu prorrogação do horário de votação e que Lula venceu por uma margem muito maior do que os votos registrados entre 17h e 19h.
A publicação estadunidense também descarta que ele esteja sofrendo qualquer tipo de perseguição, ao destacar que Flávio Bolsonaro “enfrenta diversas investigações relacionadas à lavagem de dinheiro e corrupção no Brasil” e que ele “fugiu após as autoridades brasileiras ordenarem a entrega de seus passaportes”.
“Eu já sei que o desfecho final será a minha prisão”, disse o senador fugido, alegando que o Judiciário brasileiro é “politizado” e lembrando que o ministro Alexandre de Moraes, que determinou a apreensão de seus passaportes, também mandou prender seu pai, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro.
Na sequência, o texto do jornal destaca que Jair foi preso “por tentar dar um golpe de Estado após a derrota nas eleições de 2022 para o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva”.
Flávio Bolsonaro também usou a entrevista para tentar proteger aliados que colaboraram com a fuga, após diversas notícias de ajuda de pessoas ligadas aos governos argentino de Javier Milei e estadunidense de Donald Trump.
Questionado sobre como articulou uma “viagem impressionante e secreta” de 8 mil quilômetros, o senador disse que “não houve ajuda de absolutamente ninguém, de nenhum governo”.

https://taz.de/Reform-fuer-den-Fuehrersc.title: Reform für den Führerschein: Make Fahrerlaubnis günstig again
https://taz.de/Reform-fuer-den-Fuehrersc.author: Mark Gilcher
https://taz.de/Reform-fuer-den-Fuehrersc.text:
Reform für den Führerschein: Make Fahrerlaubnis günstig again
Der Bundestag hat eine Reform des Führerscheins beschlossen. Bis zu 1.000 Euro niedrigere Kosten peilt der Verkehrsminister an. Ist das möglich?
Nicht nur billiger, sondern auch digitaler und weniger bürokratisch soll der Führerschein in Zukunft werden. Das will die Bundesregierung ab Juli 2027 mit einer Reform erreichen, deren erster Teil am Donnerstag den Bundestag passiert hat. Einige der Änderungen müssen noch durch den Bundesrat und werden durch die Länder ausgestaltet. Auch dem zweiten Teil des Reformpakets – einer Verordnung des Verkehrsministeriums – müssen die Länder noch zustimmen.
Die größte Neuheit ist die sogenannte Laienausbildung. Damit wird das Konzept des begleiteten Fahrens mit 17 ausgeweitet auf die Zeit der praktischen Ausbildung. So sollen Fahrschüler:innen mehr Fahrpraxis neben den Fahrstunden sammeln können. Dafür müssen sie bereits die theoretische Prüfung bestanden und sechs Fahrstunden absolviert haben. Die Begleitpersonen, beispielsweise Eltern, sollen ebenfalls theoretisch und praktisch vorbereitet werden.
Auch können Fahrschüler:innen den Theorieunterricht zukünftig online absolvieren. Das soll die Raumkosten der Fahrschulen senken. In der Theorieprüfung soll außerdem der Fragenkatalog deutlich reduziert werden.
Weiterhin sollen die Vorgaben für Sonderfahrten wegfallen. Bisher sind zwölf davon Pflicht, etwa bei Dunkelheit oder auf der Autobahn. Nun können Fahrlehrer:innen individuell entscheiden, wer wie viele Stunden braucht. Dazu kommen eine geringere Prüfungsdauer sowie ein Transparenzregister, mit dem Kund:innen Preise und Bestehensquoten vergleichen können.
Effekt der Führerschein-Reform noch unklar
Ob die von Bundesverkehrsminister Steffen Bilger (CDU) angekündigte Ersparnis von bis zu 1.000 Euro realistisch ist, ist umstritten. „Zum einen müssten Fahrschulen die Einsparungen weitergeben, zum anderen Fahrschüler:innen tatsächlich weniger Fahrstunden benötigen“, sagte Michael Müller-Görnert, verkehrspolitischer Sprecher des ökologischen Verkehrsclubs VCD der taz. Die Bundesvereinigung der Fahrlehrerverbände hält die Kostenreduktion für unrealistisch.
Generell sei es zu begrüßen, wenn der Führerschein günstiger wird, so Müller-Görnert. Doch solle der politische Fokus darauf liegen, Alternativen zum Auto zu stärken, etwa durch ein besseres Bus- und Bahnangebot oder ein vergünstigtes Deutschlandticket.

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/6.title: Why is Iran exempting India, China, Qatar, Iraq from Hormuz restrictions?
https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/6.text:
Why is Iran exempting India, China, Qatar, Iraq from Hormuz restrictions?
Tehran says ships from four countries can cross Hormuz freely, but analysts say the deals carry political risks.
Iran has exempted ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar from its Strait of Hormuz restrictions, a senior Iranian lawmaker said on Tuesday.
“Ships from these countries pass freely, and the Americans do not intercept them either,” Amir Hayat Moqaddam, deputy chairman of the Iranian parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, told the Iranian Students’ News Agency (ISNA).
Iran effectively shut the strait early in the US-Israel war on Iran, which began on February 28, and the United States reimposed a naval blockade on Iran’s southern ports in July.
So why have these four countries been granted passage through the critical strait, and can their ships really sail freely while the blockade remains in place?
What does Iran get in return for letting ships pass?
It will receive medicine from India and political backing from China, according to Hayat Moqaddam. Iran already receives diplomatic support from Qatar, which is leading mediation efforts to end the US-Israel war on Iran.
Hayat Moqaddam said Tehran will also collect transit fees from Indian and Chinese ships, while Qatari vessels pass free. He did not say whether Iraqi ships will pay a toll.
“Whatever the lawmaker says is the rationale – the big question is if it works and, if yes, to what extent?” Rouzbeh Parsi, an Iran analyst and affiliated researcher at Lund University’s Department of History and Human Rights Studies, told Al Jazeera.
“Iran has been under sanctions for a very long time, so bartering and quid pro quos in trade are nothing new,” he said. The difference now, he added, is that “it’s about poking holes in an embargo and getting crucial goods/services in and out”.
Nader Hashemi, an associate professor of Middle East politics at Georgetown University, said that “most likely Iran is charging a transit fee or a percentage of the cargo value to allow those ships to go through without being harassed”.
“It’s a clever move by Tehran for several reasons,” Wolfgang Pusztai, a security and defence analyst and Austria’s former defence attache to Libya, told Al Jazeera.
“If successful, this move will generate significant revenue for Iran, as China is by far the largest purchaser of Iranian crude oil, buying nearly 90 percent of Iran’s total oil exports,” he said.
By including Qatar, with its many liquefied natural gas (LNG) buyers, and India, Iran is also “trying to undermine acceptance” of Washington’s strategy in the conflict, especially as it charges Qatar no tolls, he added.
Why does it matter to these four countries?
All four are highly dependent on the Strait of Hormuz for exports.
Of the 10.23 million barrels a day of Gulf crude that passed through the strait in October, about 42 percent went to China and 13 percent to India, Muyu Xu, a senior crude oil analyst at the analytics firm Kpler, told Al Jazeera.
“China is the country most able to cross US interests. The question is whether Beijing considers it worth the potential political cost,” Parsi said.
Asia is particularly reliant on Gulf oil and gas usually shipped out via Hormuz. Countries there have much to offer in return for allowing ships to pass.
“For India, the shutdown of oil from the Gulf has been a great loss – and it is a big producer of the pharmaceuticals that Iran cannot manufacture itself,” he said.
Qatar, which is mediating between Washington and Tehran, shipped no LNG through the strait in August, but managed 1.8 million tonnes in October, Xu said.
Its crude transits fell over the same period, from 517,000 barrels a day to 193,000, while Iraq’s rose from 1.69 million to 2.65 million.
Kpler has been unable to trace the origin of up to two million barrels a day of Middle Eastern crude, so both countries’ flows may be higher, Xu said.
“India and Qatar have closer relationships with DC they need to maintain – while both of them also feel let down by Trump,” Parsi said, adding, “For Qatar, maintaining a relationship with Iran is also vital since it’s an unavoidable neighbour.”
“So for all of them, there are upsides for these exemptions from Iranian restrictions but also political dangers,” he said.
Is this announcement new?
Not entirely.
Iran began letting some vessels from countries it considers friendly pass within weeks of the war starting. And in April, its military command said “brotherly” Iraq was exempt.
With the Iraqi exemption, Iran “probably intends to support the economic recovery” of its western neighbour, a fellow Shia-majority country, Pusztai said.
Will ships be able to get past the US blockade?
That depends on Washington.
US Central Command (CENTCOM) has said the blockade applies to “all vessels of all nations entering or leaving coastal areas or ports in Iran”, while vessels avoiding Iranian ports are not affected.
It has also said humanitarian shipments, including “food and medical supplies essential for the survival of the civilian populations”, can pass after inspection.
But Hayat Moqaddam did not appear to limit the exemptions to ships trading with other Gulf states, Pusztai noted. “If this is really the case, this would also have a significant impact on the other Gulf states, including Saudi Arabia,” he said.
“This could make the continuation of the American naval blockade more difficult and less effective, assuming Washington accepts this Iranian move,” he said. The main change, he added, is that the exemption “would also cover Chinese/Indian ships from/to Iran”, if the US accepts it.
It is also unclear whether “ships of these countries” means the flag a vessel flies, its owner, its operator or some other link, Pusztai said.
Ending the blockade is one of Tehran’s demands before it will commit to broader peace talks with the US, which will include discussions about Iran’s nuclear programme. Qatar-mediated talks currently centre on an Iranian proposal to reopen the strait if the US meets seven conditions, including this and lifting sanctions.
“It seems to be that Iran tries to separate the questions of free passage through the Strait of Hormuz and oil exports from the nuclear question,” Pusztai said, adding, “The American reaction will show if this is successful.”
Will this make a difference to oil markets?
Not much, for now.
“I think they make only limited difference at present,” Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG Group, told Al Jazeera.
“Markets are back to pricing in a peace deal, but if conflict flares up at full tilt, then Iranian commanders may not have time to distinguish their targets,” he said, adding: “At present, the focus remains squarely on the prospects of a broader deal.”
An exemption has not guaranteed safety. On October 30, the Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda was struck by “unidentified objects” in the Gulf, said its owner, Qatar Gas Transport Company.
More than 120 commercial ships have been hit in the region since the war began, with October being the worst month, according to data from the International Maritime Organization and United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: ‘Samba RAP’ une batalha de rima e roda de samba em celebração à cultura negra, neste sábado (7)
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Gustavo de Sousa
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Em Curitiba (PR), a Casa Cultural Àlàáfíà, receberá o “Samba RAP: no batuque do improviso”. A ideia é conectar as expressões do samba e do rap, por meio de expressões no Paraná. A iniciativa é gratuita e reúne grupos como a banda In Versos, o artista Léo Fé, além de batalhas de rima e rodas de samba de partido-alto.
“Unir o samba de partido-alto e o rap na Casa Cultural Àlàáfíà, um quilombo urbano, revela a potência e a resistência de dois gêneros que surgiram como formas de expressão crítica. MCs e sambistas se encontram em desafios de palavras”, conta Andressa Medeiros, organizadora do evento.
O estilo de partido-alto consiste em versos que são criados nas rodas de samba, como resposta de um sambista a outro, se aproximando de uma batalha de rima. Tanto o samba quanto o hip-hop são as formas dos artistas transformarem as reivindicações em arte a partir do improviso.
“A poesia também é um instrumento de libertação e um meio de revolução”, afirma Medeiros.
O Samba RAP será das 14h às 18h. Confira a programação:
14h | Apresentação da banda In Versos
15h | Roda de samba com Léo Fé e Samba Versado, com intervenções de MCs
17h | Batalha de rima com a Associação dos Rimadores e participação da rapper Vania Rodrigues
Mais informações podem ser conferidas no instagram da Ariramba Cultural.
A banda In Versos é formada pelos artistas Diggo, OCunha, Maus e Jaketa, que misturam diferentes estilos musicais e composições autorais na abertura do evento. O artista Léo Fé e o coletivo Samba Versado conduzem uma roda de samba dedicada ao partido-alto. O encerramento terá uma batalha de rima com participação de MC Vania Rodrigues e convidados.
A MC Vania Rodrigues acumula quase duas décadas de trajetória no rap, com apresentações que incluem a abertura de um show dos Racionais MCs. O sambista Léo Fé se destaca pela atuação no samba de partido-alto no Paraná, tendo conquistado o título de campeão do 2º Festival Nacional de Samba de Partido Alto.
Serviço
Samba RAP: no batuque do improviso
Data: sábado, 7 de novembro, das 14h às 18h
Local: Casa Cultural Àlàáfíà (Av. Jaime Reis, 480 – São Francisco)
A entrada é gratuita.
*Estagiário sob supervisão de Murilo Bernardon.

https://taz.de/Diem25-in-Existenznoeten/.title: Diem25 in Existenznöten: Bank zieht bei Varoufakis den Stecker
https://taz.de/Diem25-in-Existenznoeten/.author: Marco Fründt
https://taz.de/Diem25-in-Existenznoeten/.text:
Diem25 in Existenznöten: Bank zieht bei Varoufakis den Stecker
Ein Geldinstitut in Belgien sperrt das Konto der linken Bewegung des ehemaligen griechischen Finanzministers. Diem25 droht eine existenzielle Krise.
Die linke Bewegung Diem25 hat den Zugriff auf ihr Bankkonto verloren. „Unsere Bank hat vergangene Woche, in all ihrer Weisheit, entschieden, unser Konto zu sperren“, gab Yanis Varoufakis am Dienstag über Instagram bekannt. Der ehemalige griechische Finanzminister und Wirtschaftsprofessor hatte die „Bewegung Demokratie in Europa 2025“ vor zehn Jahren in Berlin auf den Weg gebracht. Der linken paneuropäischen Bewegung Diem25 gehören Parteien in Deutschland, Frankreich, Schweden, Italien und Griechenland Parteien unter dem Namen Mera25 an.
„Die überraschende und unbegründete Schließung unseres Kontos – obwohl wir allen Verpflichtungen gemäß der ‚Know Your Customer‘-Vorschriften für Banken nachgekommen sind und durch die belgischen Behörden geprüft wurden – ist eine klare und unmittelbare Bedrohung für die europäisch Demokratie“, sagte Varoufakis der taz.
Varoufakis erlangte Bekanntheit als er 2015 vom damaligen griechischen Premier Alexis Tsipras zum Finanzminister ernannt wurde. Der erklärte Gegner der EU-Sparmaßnahmen trat wenige Monate später zurück, nachdem die Syriza-Regierung die Sparpakete angenommen hatte.
„Know Your Customer“, also „Kenne deinen Kunden“ bezeichnet gesetzlich vorgegebene Prüfverfahren, mit denen Banken sicherstellen sollen, wer hinter den Konten steht und ob die Geschäftsbeziehung und Transaktionen plausibel sind. So sollen Geldwäsche, die Finanzierung von Terrorismus, Betrug oder die Umgehung von Sanktionen verhindert werden.
Kein Zugriff mehr
Den Namen der Bank in Belgien, wo Diem25 seinen administrativen Sitz hat, wolle man derzeit nicht öffentlich machen, sagte Erik Edman, politischer Direktor von Diem25, der taz. Erstmals habe die Vereinigung am 8. Oktober bemerkt, dass sie keinen Zugriff auf ihr Bankguthaben gehabt habe.
Die Bank habe daraufhin mitgeteilt, bereits Wochen vorher postalisch angekündigt zu haben, das Konto zum Juli zu kündigen, jedoch eine dreimonatige Frist einzuräumen. Einen Brief habe es allerdings nie gegeben, behauptet Edman. Die folgenden Einsprüche habe die Bank ignoriert. Von einem Tag auf den anderen habe die Bewegung keinen Zugriff mehr auf ihr Geld gehabt.
„Für unsere Bewegung ist das eine existenzielle Krise, da alle unsere Ausgaben und Gehälter über dieses Konto gedeckt wurden“, sagte Edman. Vorerst versuche man, über einen Notfallspendenfonds die Grundausgaben zu decken. Die Eröffnung eines neuen Bankkontos habe sich zudem als schwierig erwiesen. „Heute haben weitaus mehr Banken Bedenken hinsichtlich des internationalen Charakters unserer Organisation als bei unserer Gründung 2016.“
Die Bank selbst habe sich bisher geweigert, Gründe für die Kontoschließung zu nennen. „Nach einer Reihe von Treffen mit Verbündeten in Belgien, die von ähnlichen Maßnahmen zur Kontosperrung betroffen waren, scheint sich jedoch ein besorgniserregender Trend abzuzeichnen“, sagte Edman.
Geschütztes Recht
Berichte über die Sperrung von Konten linker Akteur:innen und Gruppen, sogenanntes Debanking, häufen sich: Anfang 2026 wurde in Berlin-Treptow das Postbank-Konto der VVN-BdA (Vereinigung der Verfolgten des Naziregimes – Bund der Antifaschistinnen und Antifaschisten) gesperrt – eine Neueröffnung bei der Berliner Sparkasse wurde nach mehrwöchiger Prüfung zunächst ohne Angabe von Gründen verweigert.
Auf öffentlichen Druck hin lenkte die Sparkasse später ein. Noch prominenter war der Fall der Roten Hilfe Ende 2025. Die GLS-Bank hatte der Rechtshilfeorganisation damals ohne Ankündigung alle Konten gekündigt, nachdem die Trump-Regierung linke Aktivist:innen auf eine Terrorliste gesetzt hatte, die von der Roten Hilfe Rechtsbeistand erhalten hatten.
Der Zugang zu einem privaten Bankkonto ist in der EU ein geschütztes Recht. Diem25 fordert, dieses Recht auch auf gemeinnützige Vereinigungen auszuweiten. „Der Zugang zu Bankdienstleistungen darf nicht als Druckmittel missbraucht werden“, so Edman.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Zucco enfrenta enxurrada de críticas por anunciar fim da Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Rural
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Marcelo Ferreira
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
O anúncio de extinção da Secretaria de Desenvolvimento Rural (SDR), com a incorporação das atribuições à Secretaria da Agricultura, está mobilizando movimentos do campo, entidades de agricultores, comunidades quilombolas e servidores para pressionar o governador eleito do Rio Grande do Sul, Luciano Zucco (PL), a recuar. As organizações denunciam o risco de subordinar a agricultura familiar às prioridades do agronegócio e cobram a manutenção da secretaria, com autonomia, orçamento e equipes próprias.
As entidades também questionam a justificativa de economia de recursos e alertam para a perda de prioridade das políticas em meio a eventos climáticos extremos que ameaçam a agricultura familiar. Na avaliação delas, a mudança pode dificultar a recuperação das propriedades e deixar em segundo plano demandas de assentados, indígenas, quilombolas e pescadores artesanais.
Está prevista para sexta-feira (6), na sede da Federação dos Trabalhadores na Agricultura no Rio Grande do Sul (Fetag-RS), em Porto Alegre, uma reunião do futuro secretário da Agricultura, Paulo Herrmann, com representantes da entidade. A fusão das pastas e a preservação das políticas para a produção familiar estão entre os temas da agenda.
Herrmann foi anunciado em 27 de outubro para comandar a pasta que absorverá o Desenvolvimento Rural. Ex-presidente da fabricante de máquinas agrícolas John Deere no Brasil, cargo ocupado entre 2012 e 2022, tem mais de 40 anos de atuação no agronegócio.
MST cobra atendimento aos assentamentos
A direção estadual do Movimento dos Trabalhadores Rurais Sem Terra (MST) repudia o anúncio e defende a SDR como principal porta de acesso, na estrutura estadual, às políticas de reforma agrária e agricultura familiar.
“Somos as famílias assentadas e camponesas que produzem alimentos saudáveis, de base agroecológica, e garantimos comida de qualidade na mesa da população gaúcha. Somos, como afirmamos, os grandes responsáveis pela produção de alimento e por um rural com gente, muito mais do que meros números e estatísticas econômicas”, afirma o movimento.
“O Rio Grande do Sul precisa avançar em diversas demandas de atendimento às famílias assentadas, esquecidas nos últimos dois governos de Eduardo Leite. Em vez de reduzir a estrutura pública voltada ao campo, o estado tem o dever de fortalecê-la para enfrentar esse passivo”, afirma a direção estadual, em nota.
O MST também argumenta que a articulação com o Ministério do Desenvolvimento Agrário e Agricultura Familiar (MDA) amplia as possibilidades de investimentos e parcerias e exige uma estrutura estadual dedicada.
“Exigimos do futuro governo a manutenção da SDR e o compromisso com a Reforma Agrária, a agroecologia e a produção de alimentos saudáveis”, reivindica o movimento.
MPA critica prioridade ao agronegócio e promete pressão
Para Miqueli Schiavon, dirigente estadual e coordenador do Movimento dos Pequenos Agricultores (MPA) no Rio Grande do Sul, o anúncio provoca frustração entre as famílias camponesas e sinaliza a orientação política da futura gestão. Ele associa a decisão a um “governo neoliberal que defende basicamente o agronegócio” e critica o discurso de que a agricultura não tem tamanho. “Isso é um horror para a agricultura familiar”, afirma.
A escolha de Herrmann reforça a preocupação do movimento. “Foi presidente da John Deere, então o currículo dele já diz para quem ele vem”, afirma Schiavon. Na avaliação do dirigente, a perda de uma estrutura própria também pode deixar a agricultura familiar gaúcha em descompasso com as políticas do governo federal.
Schiavon lembra que a secretaria foi uma conquista da mobilização do setor e relata que, no período anterior em que a área ficou sem pasta própria, políticas foram paralisadas. Segundo ele, as demandas foram remetidas a um departamento onde “tudo ficou no segundo plano”.
A recriação da SDR, segundo ele, permitiu retomar programas, embora com recursos inferiores aos reivindicados pelo movimento.
O MPA pretende manter a mobilização para tentar mudar a decisão. “A gente vai continuar fazendo pressão para que o governador volte atrás, mesmo sabendo que essa possibilidade é muito remota”, afirma Schiavon.
Fetraf questiona economia e continuidade dos programas
A Federação dos Trabalhadores na Agricultura Familiar do Rio Grande do Sul (Fetraf-RS) classifica a extinção da pasta independente como um equívoco político e econômico e pede que Zucco reveja a decisão.
O coordenador-geral da federação, Douglas Cenci, questiona como o futuro governo pretende garantir que os programas cheguem às propriedades. A preocupação parte de dificuldades que, segundo a entidade, já existiam no acesso às políticas estaduais mesmo com uma secretaria específica.
Na nota oficial, a Fetraf-RS rejeita a ideia de que a manutenção da pasta possa ser avaliada apenas como despesa administrativa. “A existência da SDR ao longo dos anos permitiu que fossem captados recursos e executados programas que em muito superaram os seus custos”, sustenta.
A federação cobra garantias para a interlocução com o MDA e destaca a diversidade dos públicos atendidos, de agricultores e assentados a comunidades tradicionais, agroindústrias familiares e cooperativas.
“A Agricultura Familiar precisa de reconhecimento, investimento e políticas públicas permanentes, e não de menos espaços institucionais”, afirma a Fetraf-RS.
A federação também contesta o momento escolhido para a reorganização: “Extinguir a SDR num momento marcado pelas mudanças climáticas mostra-se um erro, visto que comprovadamente os eventos atingem sobremaneira o setor, exigindo do estado do Rio Grande do Sul investimentos com o foco em auxiliar na resiliência aos efeitos desses eventos climáticos”.
Servidores alertam para perda de autonomia
A Associação dos Servidores das Ciências Agrárias do Rio Grande do Sul (Assagra) também pede a revisão da medida. Em nota assinada pelo presidente Paulo Henrique Souza da Silva, a entidade alerta que o Desenvolvimento Rural pode perder protagonismo ao ser absorvido por uma secretaria que já responde por fiscalização sanitária, defesa agropecuária, inspeção e outras atribuições.
“Não basta preservar atribuições no papel: é necessário garantir estrutura, orçamento, equipes técnicas e autonomia para que as políticas públicas cheguem efetivamente a quem mais precisa”, afirma a associação.
Para a Assagra, a permanência de famílias e jovens no campo também é resultado do investimento público, mesmo quando não aparece nas planilhas financeiras.
“A administração pública não pode ser conduzida exclusivamente pela lógica da administração empresarial”, sustenta a entidade. “Enxugar a máquina pública não pode significar enfraquecer políticas essenciais”, acrescenta.
“O fortalecimento da agricultura familiar, dos povos indígenas, das comunidades quilombolas e dos pequenos produtores precisa ser uma política permanente de Estado, e não uma atividade secundária dentro de uma estrutura administrativa mais abrangente”, reivindica a Assagra.
A entidade também questiona a repetição de uma reorganização que já foi revertida no passado. “Será que não aprendemos com os erros do passado? Por que repetir uma decisão cuja experiência já demonstrou a importância de ser revista?”, indaga a associação.
Quilombolas denunciam falta de consulta
O Fórum das Comunidades Quilombolas do Litoral Médio do Rio Grande do Sul denuncia a falta de participação das populações tradicionais na decisão e defende a manutenção da SDR.
A articulação, que reúne comunidades de Mostardas, Tavares, São José do Norte, Palmares do Sul e Capivari do Sul, lançou um abaixo-assinado pela manutenção da secretaria.
“Para nossas comunidades, o desenvolvimento rural não pode ser compreendido apenas como produção agropecuária ou crescimento econômico”, afirma o fórum. A articulação relaciona o tema aos direitos territoriais, à soberania alimentar, aos saberes tradicionais e à permanência digna das famílias.
“Não podemos admitir que essas populações sejam tratadas como questões secundárias na organização das políticas de desenvolvimento do Estado”, pontua.
O fórum denuncia a falta de escuta das comunidades. “É alarmante o completo desrespeito à consulta prévia, livre e informada”, afirma, ao criticar a decisão tomada sem a participação dessas populações.
A manifestação invoca a Convenção 169 da Organização Internacional do Trabalho (OIT), que prevê consulta aos povos interessados, por meio das instituições representativas, diante de medidas legislativas ou administrativas suscetíveis de afetá-los diretamente.
O fórum cobra do governo estadual e da Assembleia Legislativa um processo de escuta antes da alteração da estrutura, além de garantias para as equipes, o orçamento e a continuidade dos projetos.
“A redução de estruturas administrativas não pode ser avaliada exclusivamente pelo número de cargos ou pelas despesas formalmente eliminadas”, sustenta a manifestação. Para a articulação quilombola, é preciso considerar os custos sociais, a perda de capacidade de planejamento e os riscos de descontinuidade das políticas.
Fetag também defende secretaria própria
A defesa da manutenção da SDR também foi apresentada inclusive pela Fetag-RS. Em nota de 27 de outubro, a federação manifestou preocupação com a fusão e reivindicou uma pasta própria, com orçamento, equipe técnica e condições de executar políticas para a agricultura e a pecuária familiar.
“A busca por eficiência administrativa deve estar acompanhada de critérios transparentes e da avaliação dos impactos sobre os serviços prestados”, afirma a Fetag-RS. A entidade também cobra preservação da capacidade técnica, continuidade dos programas e participação das organizações representativas na reorganização.
A Fetag-RS solicitou reunião com Zucco e a equipe de transição antes da definição da nova estrutura.
Um setor majoritário em número de estabelecimentos
A dimensão da agricultura familiar ajuda a explicar a abrangência da reação. O Censo Agropecuário de 2017, do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE), identificou 293.892 estabelecimentos familiares no Rio Grande do Sul, equivalentes a 80,5% do total.
Esses estabelecimentos reuniam 716.695 pessoas ocupadas, cerca de 72,2% do pessoal ocupado na agropecuária estadual naquele ano.
As atribuições da SDR ultrapassam o incentivo à produção agrícola: incluem políticas para pecuaristas familiares, mulheres e juventude rural, comunidades quilombolas, indígenas, assentados, pescadores e aquicultores, além de cooperativismo, agroecologia e desenvolvimento territorial.
Entre as ações vinculadas à pasta estão o apoio às agroindústrias familiares e a Operação Terra Forte, voltada à recuperação dos solos e à resiliência climática.
A proposta de incorporação também retoma uma experiência anterior. A SDR deixou de existir como pasta independente na reorganização para o primeiro governo de Eduardo Leite (PSD) e foi recriada no início do segundo mandato, em 2023, após aprovação legislativa no final de 2022. Tanto o MPA quanto a Assagra recorrem a esse histórico para questionar a repetição da mudança.
Zucco promete manter apoio, mas não detalha estrutura
Em nota encaminhada pela assessoria ao Brasil de Fato RS, o governo eleito afirma que a integração das secretarias “não representará qualquer redução nas políticas públicas ou no apoio destinado à agricultura familiar do Rio Grande do Sul”.
A justificativa é tornar a gestão mais eficiente e considerar a situação financeira do estado. O texto invoca o compromisso de campanha e o resultado eleitoral como respaldo à medida.
Segundo a assessoria, a futura Secretaria da Agricultura deverá atender todo o setor produtivo ligado ao agro, “respeitando as particularidades e necessidades de cada segmento, sem distinções”. A nota reconhece a importância econômica e social da agricultura familiar e afirma que Zucco atuou em defesa dos produtores, inclusive em relação ao endividamento rural.
O governo eleito também informa que Zucco e Herrmann deverão se reunir com representantes da agricultura familiar para ouvir demandas, receber sugestões e construir as prioridades da gestão.
A manifestação não especifica se haverá uma subsecretaria exclusiva, quais recursos e equipes estarão reservados à área nem como será assegurada autonomia para executar os programas. Também não apresenta o valor que o governo espera economizar com a incorporação.

https://taz.de/Erster-Migra-Streik-in-Ha.author: Timo Krügener
https://taz.de/Erster-Migra-Streik-in-Ha.text:
Erster Migra-Streik in Halle: Täglich angefeindet
In Halle haben am Donnerstag rund 30 Migrant*innen ihre Geschäfte geschlossen. Es ist ein Protest gegen den zunehmenden Rassismus in Sachsen-Anhalt.
Am Donnerstagmorgen muss Wael Alomar dringend noch ein paar Anrufe tätigen, denn über die Website seines Restaurants kommen Bestellungen rein. Was die Bestellenden nicht wissen: Bei Alomar gibt es heute kein Essen. Er macht mit beim ersten sogenannten Migra-Streik in Halle. Neben Alomar beteiligen sich laut Organisator*innen rund 30 weitere Geschäfte an dem Streik. Gemeinsam wollen sie angesichts einer zunehmend migrationsfeindlichen Stimmung im Land ein sichtbares Zeichen setzen.
Sie wollen deutlich machen, dass Halle ohne Menschen mit Migrationsgeschichte nicht die „vielfältige, schöne und lebenswerte Stadt“ wäre, die sie ist. So steht es im Aufruf. Von der zunehmend negativen Stimmung gegenüber Menschen, die migrantisch gelesen werden, kann auch Alomar berichten. Angehörige seiner Familie würden seit der Landtagswahl im September täglich rassistische Anfeindungen erfahren. In der Schule, im Supermarkt und sogar auf dem Marktplatz.
Diskriminierung und Faschismus habe er schon in seinem Herkunftsland Syrien erlebt – und dieses 2008 verlassen. Er wolle nicht umziehen, sagt Alomar. Aber wenn es so weitergehe, bleibe ihm keine Wahl, dann würde er Sachsen-Anhalt verlassen. „Wir sind nach Deutschland gekommen, weil wir Schutz gesucht haben“, sagt er: „Und wenn der Rechtsstaat uns diesen nicht garantieren kann, können wir nicht bleiben.“
Vor knapp drei Wochen berichtete das Landesnetzwerk Migrantenorganisationen in Sachsen-Anhalt (Lamsa) in der Bundespressekonferenz, seit der Landtagswahl im Schnitt täglich rassistische Übergriffe zu erfassen. Aus eben solchen Übergriffen sei die Idee zum Streik entstanden, erklärt in Halle einer der Organisierenden von der Initiative „MigraStark“. Aus Sicherheitsgründen soll sein echter Name nicht veröffentlicht werden, er heißt in diesem Text Beşîr Rojava.
Rassistische Flyer und Bedrohungen
Er habe mit Menschen gesprochen, die schon am Wahlabend blaue Abschiebe-Flugtickets in ihren Briefkästen gehabt hätten, berichtet Rojava. Familienangehörige und Freund*innen würden einen deutlichen Zuwachs an rassistischen Vorfällen wahrnehmen. Im Gespräch mit Gewerbebetreibenden sei dann der Vorschlag aufgekommen, in Halle einen Migra-Streik zu organisieren, wie es ihn in Magdeburg vor der Landtagswahl gab.
Doch viele Gewerbebetreibenden hätten im Vorfeld Angst gehabt, in den Fokus von Diskriminierungen zu rücken, Kunden zu verlieren und finanzielle Verluste oder zerschlagene Fensterscheiben zu erleiden, berichtet Rojava. Fast täglich sei er deshalb gemeinsam mit Unterstützer*innen des Streiks von Geschäft zu Geschäft gelaufen und habe versucht, die Menschen zu überzeugen, sich dem Streik anzuschließen.
Widerständig zu sein, wenn Unrecht geschieht, habe er als Kurde mit der Muttermilch aufgenommen, sagt Rojava – denn „Widerstand ist Leben“. Der Streik solle Menschen aus der migrantischen Community dazu ermutigen, nicht stillschweigend zuzuschauen, während rassistische Übergriffe von Tag zu Tag mehr würden. „Deine Rechte wird dir niemand schenken“, sagt Rojava.
Nur ein Anfang
Erst hatte er Sorge, dass sich kaum Gewerbetreibende beteiligen. Nun haben sich doch deutlich mehr Menschen angeschlossen. Einige wären sogar am Morgen noch spontan dazugekommen. Am besten habe der Streik dort funktioniert, wo die Gewerbebetreibenden miteinander ins Gespräch gekommen sind, sagt Rojava. Wenn ein Laden streike, schlössen sich andere an. Genauso habe er aber in manchen Straßen beobachtet, dass Läden, die eine Teilnahme zugesichert hatten, nun doch geöffnet haben, weil ihre Nachbarläden nicht schließen.
Rojava ist auch angesichts der Kundgebung am Steintor mit rund 200 Menschen hoffnungsvoll, dass der heutige Tag nur ein Anfang ist und sie auf der Vernetzung und dem Erfolg aufbauen können. „Mit dem Streik zeigen wir, was dieser Gesellschaft fehlt, sollten wir weg sein“, sagt auch Restaurantbesitzer Alomar.
Der Schutz von Menschen dürfe jedoch nicht an ihren Nutzen gekoppelt sein, sagt Rojava. Die migrationsfeindliche Politik und die rassistische Hetze hätten Folgen für alle Menschen in dieser Gesellschaft. „Ausgrenzung und Anfeindungen richten sich auf der Straße nicht nach Anstellungsverhältnis, sondern nach Aussehen, Sprache und Herkunft aus.“

https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/6.text:
US Justice Department sues Penn State over undocumented students’ tuition
The lawsuit challenges Penn State’s policy that allows undocumented students to qualify for reduced tuition rates.
The United States Department of Justice has sued Pennsylvania State University, accusing the institution of violating federal law by offering in-state tuition rates to undocumented students while denying the same reduced rates to all US citizens.
The lawsuit, filed on Thursday, argues that the university’s tuition policy discriminates against citizens.
Currently, undocumented students can qualify for in-state tuition if they meet Penn State’s residency standards.
But prosecutors have rejected that policy, saying it violates a federal law that bars “preferential treatment” in higher education for undocumented immigrants, unless the same benefits are available to US citizens.
In the US, public universities typically charge lower tuition to students who are residents of the state where the institution is located, while students from other states pay higher rates.
Proponents of such policies say in-state tuition helps prevent “brain drain”, wherein students might leave the state to attend universities elsewhere. They also reward residents of the state, who contribute taxes to the education system.
Advocates argue the same benefits should be directed towards undocumented students, who are often brought to the country as minors. Making undocumented students eligible for in-state tuition can also reduce the barriers they face to education.
But the Justice Department is seeking a court order preventing Penn State from continuing to offer in-state tuition rates to undocumented students, including those living in Pennsylvania, regardless of their immigration status.
It is also seeking to block the university from adopting future tuition policies that give undocumented students “preferential treatment” over US citizens.
“Congress made a deliberate policy choice that states and their public institutions may not grant tuition benefits to illegal aliens unless those same benefits are made to all US citizens,” Brett Shumate, assistant attorney general of the Justice Department’s Civil Division, said in a statement.
The lawsuit is part of a broader campaign under President Donald Trump to challenge state policies granting reduced tuition to undocumented students.
Since returning to office for a second term in 2025, Trump has sought to clamp down on undocumented immigration, promising to lead the largest deportation effort in US history.
The Justice Department said Thursday’s filing brings the total number of lawsuits it has brought challenging such policies to 27. It also said six cases in Texas, Kentucky, Oklahoma, Nebraska, Illinois and Kansas resulted in court orders permanently blocking similar tuition policies.
In Thursday’s lawsuit, prosecutors called such policies unconstitutional. They also argued that laws like the 1996 Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act ban “public benefits from serving as an incentive” for undocumented immigration.
“Federal law prohibits illegal aliens from being eligible to receive postsecondary education benefits based on residence within a state if such benefits are denied to US citizens residing in other states,” the lawsuit said.
“There are no exceptions. Yet, Pennsylvania State University has ignored this congressional prohibition.”
According to Penn State’s current residency requirements, non-citizen applicants must have attended an accredited Pennsylvania high school for at least four years and graduated from one to qualify for in-state tuition.
Penn State said it was aware of the complaint and was reviewing it.

https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.title: Brasil condena bloqueio dos EUA a Cuba em cúpula em Madri: ‘Era da diplomacia da força já passou’
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.author: Redação
https://www.brasildefato.com.br/2026/11/.text:
Os chanceleres do Brasil, de Cuba, México, Uruguai e Nicarágua condenaram o bloqueio econômico dos Estados Unidos contra Cuba durante a 30ª Cúpula Ibero-Americana, encerrada nesta quinta-feira (5) em Madri, na Espanha. Os diplomatas se posicionaram contra as medidas endurecidas pelo governo de Donald Trump nos últimos meses, como um cerco energético que deixou a ilha sem combustível.
Representante do Brasil no encontro, o ministro das Relações Exteriores, Mauro Vieira, afirmou que o país se opõe com firmeza ao embargo econômico, comercial e financeiro e às ações de Washington para cortar ilegalmente o fornecimento de energia a Cuba. “Os Estados Unidos têm adotado ações que atingem os mais vulneráveis, prejudicando o desenvolvimento sustentável de Cuba”, criticou.
“Desde a comunidade ibero-americana, não podemos aceitar os retrocessos. Não podemos nos conformar com ameaças ao importante acervo de conquistas básicas de nossos países”, declarou Vieira.
O chanceler defendeu uma ordem internacional baseada no multilateralismo, e não em hegemonias. “O Brasil vai continuar a apoiar a visão de que a ordem mundial do século 21 está assentada nas virtudes do equilíbrio de poder e do multilateralismo, e não em ações obsoletas de hegemonia e esferas de influência”, sustentou. “A era das arrogâncias unilaterais, dos protetorados e da diplomacia da força já passou”, acrescentou.
Vieira também retomou o discurso do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva na última Assembleia Geral da Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU), em setembro. “Somos chamados a optar entre o multilateralismo ou o unilateralismo, a democracia ou o extremismo, a soberania ou a subordinação”, lembrou o chanceler, citando o petista. “O Brasil não cabe no quintal de ninguém”, completou, recorrendo a outra frase de Lula.
Para o ministro, a coesão entre os países da região é condição para enfrentar esse cenário. “Se estivermos mais coesos, teremos mais autonomia e peso”, ressaltou.
Cerco energético
O chanceler cubano, Bruno Rodríguez, detalhou o impacto das medidas adotadas por Washington ao longo deste ano. “Durante os últimos dez meses, o povo cubano sofreu o reforço sem precedentes do bloqueio econômico estadunidense, a imposição de um cerco energético equivalente a um bloqueio naval e a aplicação de sanções secundárias a indivíduos ou entidades que estabeleçam relações comerciais com Cuba”, relatou.
“Os Estados Unidos levaram sua obsessiva guerra econômica contra Cuba a limites desumanos de castigo coletivo”, denunciou Rodríguez, que agradeceu aos países ibero-americanos que votaram a favor da resolução contra o bloqueio aprovada pela Assembleia Geral da Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU) na semana passada.
O chanceler avaliou que o mundo vive um momento marcado pelo unilateralismo e pela “pretensão imperialista e inviável de impor a paz por meio da força”, como definiu, e cobrou que a conferência preserve sua autonomia. “Isso só será possível se defendermos com determinação a atuação independente da Conferência Ibero-Americana, sem ingerências, exclusões nem pressões externas”, afirmou. “Diante da arbitrariedade e do uso abusivo do poder imperialista, devemos agir de acordo com os princípios fundacionais da comunidade”, defendeu.
Rodríguez resgatou ainda perguntas feitas por Fidel Castro na cúpula de Santiago do Chile, há 30 anos, que, segundo ele, seguem sem resposta. “Se fecharmos os olhos e não agirmos com a unidade, a lucidez e a energia que este momento crucial da nossa história exige, o que será de nossos Estados no século 21? O que restará da nossa independência?”, questionou, citando o líder da Revolução Cubana.
Posição histórica do México
Pelo México, o secretário de Relações Exteriores, Roberto Velasco, abriu o discurso com uma mensagem da presidenta do país. “Trago a esta cúpula a saudação fraterna da presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, a primeira mulher que governa o México e a voz de um povo que decidiu mudar o rumo de sua história”, disse.
Velasco reafirmou os princípios da política externa mexicana. “Acreditamos no entendimento entre nações soberanas, no direito internacional, na democracia, na autodeterminação dos povos e na solução pacífica das controvérsias, princípios que nossa Constituição consagra e que hoje valem mais do que nunca”, declarou. “Por isso, reiteramos nossa posição histórica de rejeição ao embargo e a outras medidas econômicas coercitivas contra Cuba”, concluiu.
Também se manifestaram contra o bloqueio os chanceleres do Uruguai, Mario Lubetkin, e da Nicarágua, Valdrack Jaentschke.
Divisão na região
O tema foi o ponto mais difícil de negociar na Declaração de Madri, documento final da cúpula. O texto não cita o bloqueio expressamente, mas inclui um trecho que rejeita a coerção entre Estados. Argentina, Colômbia, Costa Rica e Paraguai se desmarcaram desse parágrafo. Na edição anterior do encontro, realizada em Cuenca, no Equador, em 2024, a declaração final saiu sem consenso.
Os mesmos quatro países estiveram entre os que votaram contra a resolução da ONU pelo fim do bloqueio, ao lado do Equador e dos Estados Unidos. Chile, Honduras e Peru se abstiveram. A resolução foi aprovada com 130 votos a favor, incluindo o do Brasil, 17 contrários e 25 abstenções, o menor apoio a Cuba em 30 anos. A queda é atribuída à pressão do governo Trump sobre países aliados.

https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/n.title: Dolly Parton’s manager drops complaint accusing nephew of harassment
https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/n.author: Associated Press
https://www.theguardian.com/music/2026/n.text:
Dolly Parton’s longtime manager on Thursday dropped a complaint that accused the late singer’s nephew of threatening her estate and its employees.
She’s Alive, the entity founded to manage and protect Parton’s estate, had secured a temporary restraining order against Bryan Seaver and his security company, Squadron Augmented Protection Services, in September.
A hearing, pushed several times over the course of a month, was slated for Tuesday.
A very brief filing in a Tennessee court Thursday gave no reason why the complaint was being withdrawn.
It said only that a proposed order was being drafted for the judge’s approval to dismiss the case without prejudice, meaning it can be refiled again. A court filing from a day earlier said the two sides had reached an agreement, but that also gave no details.
The Associated Press sent emails seeking comment from lawyers for She’s Alive, Seaver and his company.
The case exposed a serious rift in Parton‘s inner circle that spilled into public view in the weeks after her death.
She’s Alive terminated Seaver and SAPS in early September, and the following week petitioned for the restraining order against him, arguing that his “terrorizing conduct made their continued retention untenable”.
The petition said that starting shortly before Parton’s 25 August death and continuing after, Seaver made threats and aimed them directly at She’s Alive’s “personnel, counsel, and business partners. In writing, he vowed to ‘destroy the entire brand.’”
It says he “called himself ‘literally an international arms dealer and mercenary’” and said everyone “needs to be worried about what I might do”.
In granting the temporary order, Chancellor I’Ashea L Myles cited Seaver’s “claimed access to weapons, experience with violence, and intention to retaliate”.
Seaver said in court filings that he considered Danny Nozell, Parton’s longtime manager, a close friend and ally before Nozell took out the restraining order.
In an affidavit, Seaver said text messages Nozell cited as evidence of his threats were a “private conversation between two friends who were both frustrated, grieving and discussing strategy”.
“I have never threatened physical harm to Mr Nozell, to any SAL employee, contractor, attorney, advisor, or business partner, or to anyone else associated with SAL,” Seaver said. “I have no intention of doing so.”

https://taz.de/Spekulationen-ueber-Melan.text:
Spekulationen über Melania Trump: Eine First Lady in Teilzeit
Als erste First Lady hat Melania Trump eine Waffenruhe ausgehandelt. Der ukrainische Präsident Selenskyj würdigt diesen Erfolg mit einem Orden.
An Melania Trump scheiden sich die Geister. Am Mittwoch hat der ukrainische Präsident Wolodymyr Selenskyj die Gattin seines US-Kollegen mit dem Orden der Fürstin Olga erster Klasse ausgezeichnet. Er zeigt damit die Dankbarkeit der Ukraine für die von Melania Trump ausgehandelte Waffenruhe und teilweise Evakuierung der von Russland eingekesselten Frontstadt Oleschky.
Der Orden ist die höchste Auszeichnung, die nur an Frauen vergeben wird. In dem Selenskyj-Dekret heißt es zur Begründung, Trump erhalte die Auszeichnung für ihren „bedeutenden persönlichen Beitrag zur humanitären Unterstützung der Ukraine, ihr aktives Engagement für Menschenrechte und wohltätige Aktivitäten zum Schutz ukrainischer Kinder“.
Melania Trump hatte nach einem Bericht der Nachrichtenagentur AP wochenlang mit Unterhändlern Russlands und der Ukraine verhandelt, um die seit Monaten nicht mehr mit Wasser, Nahrungsmitteln, Medikamenten und Treibstoff versorgten Menschen in Oleschky zu beliefern. Und allen dort, die gehen wollen, die Ausreise in die Ukraine oder nach Russland zu ermöglichen. Das war etwa 800 Menschen am Sonnabend gelungen.
Melania Trump ist damit die erste Präsidentengattin, die eine Waffenruhe ausgehandelt hat. Zuvor hatte sie als erste First Lady in der Geschichte der Vereinten Nationen eine Sitzung des UN-Sicherheitsrates geleitet. An diesem Donnerstag will sie Details zu der Rettungsaktion in Oleschky berichten. Ob sie dabei auch etwas zu ihren Bemühungen um die Freilassung der Zehntausenden nach Russland verschleppten ukrainischen Kinder sagt, bleibt zunächst unklar.
Weniger öffentliche Auftritte
Damit zeigt sich die 1970 in der damals noch zu Jugoslawien gehörenden slowenischen Kleinstadt Sevnica Aufgewachsene erstmals wieder der Öffentlichkeit. Die Wahlnacht der Midterms hatte sie nach Presseberichten nicht an der Seite ihres Mannes Donald Trump und dessen Beratern im Weißen Haus verbracht.
Laut einer Analyse des TV-Kanals NBC hatte Melania in der zweiten Trump-Amtszeit nur halb so viele öffentliche Auftritte wie in Donald Trumps ersten vier Jahren. Melania Trump, die einst bei von US-Medien berichteten Ehekrisen gesagt hatte, „Ich weiß, wen ich geheiratet habe“, macht sich rar. „Ich habe gehört, ihr habt mich vermisst. Hier bin ich“, sagte die 56-Jährige am 20. August, als sie im Rosengarten des Weißen Hauses nach 32-tägiger Abstinenz die von ihr entwickelte Initiative zur Unterstützung von Pflegekindern vorstellte.
Im Oktober setzte sie beim Präsidentengatten eine Initiative für Frauengesundheit durch. Aktuell macht sie Schutz von Kindern vor künstlicher Intelligenz zu einem Kernthema. Über das 1995 nach New York übergesiedelten Model Melania Knauss, seit Januar 2005 mit Trump verheiratet, gehen die Meinungen auseinander: Die New York Times nannte sie „die slowenische Sphinx“. In der Los Angeles Times wurde sie indes als „politische Akteurin, die keine Kompromisse kennt“ bezeichnet. Und laut New Yorker sei sie „mindestens so imperial wie ihr Mann“.
Sie selbst hatte in der Zeit, als ihr Mann wegen einer Schweigegeldaffäre um seine Liaison mit der Pornodarstellerin Stormy Daniels vor Gericht stand, CNN gesagt: Die Leute würden denken „Oh, arme Melania.“ Aber sie sage den Leuten: „Habt kein Mitleid mit mir. Ich kann damit umgehen.“
Hohe Verluste
Seit Trumps erster Wahl spekulieren die Medien, ob sie Rätsel, Opfer oder Komplizin sei. Im Ergebnis jedenfalls sei laut Trump-Biograf Michael Wolff ein Firmenimperium mit 17 Millionen Dollar Gewinn entstanden, davon mehr als 10 Millionen Dollar Erlöse aus dem von Amazon finanzierten Film „Melania“. Der mit 40 Millionen Dollar teuerste je in Auftrag gegebene Dokumentarfilm spielte hohe Verluste ein und wurde als „berechnend, wütend machend und entsetzlich“ verrissen.
Wegen ihrer Rückzüge aus der Öffentlichkeit, während über ihren Gatten wegen möglicherweise zu enger Beziehungen zu seiner Assistentin Natalie Harp oder zuletzt erneut über Vergewaltigungsvorwürfe berichtet wird, wird Melania als „Teilzeit-First-Lady“ bezeichnet. Sie ist laut CNN die unbeliebteste First Lady aller Zeiten. Allerdings wussten da die Befragten noch nicht, dass sie eine Waffenruhe und die Rettung von 800 Menschen erreicht hat.
